checks: Translation by tv changes the old threshold on the one moving fiber by −t u_j·v and preserves its volume exactly. Thus the captured derivative is S_j(z)u_j·v, with no total mass term.

For a proper trace the unit-normal coarea integral and proper-section continuity give this derivative. When the cut is strictly exterior or supporting with surface-null face, nearby translated sections eventually lie in arbitrarily small neighborhoods of the projected limiting trace. Their areas tend to zero. A supporting interval endpoint is excluded by the stated regularity.

Neutrality in all translations makes (θ_j S_j(z))_j a kernel vector of the normals. Minimal positive dependence gives the one-dimensional kernel span of ρ. Substituting θ_j proportional to ρ_j/S_j with S_j>0 yields S_j(z)/S_j constant and hence the stated all-or-none proper statuses.
Read 00208e2b45f0da1a §4. This argument uses neutrality as a hypothesis and does not infer it for multiple circuits or for a supporting-facet coincidence.

dependencies.hypotheses: The accepted proper-section continuity applies to a fixed compact full-dimensional fiber with the same nonzero unit normal and threshold approaching an interior support level. The nonproper zero derivatives are justified separately by the surface-null limiting trace.

overlap.comparison: The accepted contact stationarity identifies full mixed section centroids under regular projected-contact conditions, not a common fiberwise coarea fraction under independent translation.

Its joint stress relates effective full section coareas and section-base barycenters, including support allocations. It does not identify all individual fiberwise ratios in this regular translation-neutral setting.

readability: Positive coarea for the full circuit and excluded supporting facets are essential for the ratio and status statements.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: An independently movable fiber contributes one common proportion of full proper coarea to every cap of a neutral minimal positive circuit.
